<hi type="bold"> saber </hi> <div eID="gen5001" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5002" type="x-p"/> Apostasía, Resumen: La apostasía, "apostarse", es el acto de cristianos profesos que deliberadamente rechazan la verdad revelada <div eID="gen5002" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) en cuanto a la deidad de Jesucristo y </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) la redención a través de Su sacrificio expiatorio y redentor <reference osisRef="1jo 4:1-3"> 1 Juan 4:1-3 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="php 3:18"> Filipenses 3:18 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:1"> 2 Pedro 2:1 </reference> . La apostasía se diferencia del error respecto a la verdad, que puede ser resultado de la ignorancia <reference osisRef="ac 19:1-6"> Hechos 19:1-6 </reference> o de la herejía, que puede deberse a la esfera de Satanás <reference osisRef="2ti 2:25 2ti 2:26"> 2 Timoteo 2:25,26 </reference> ambas pueden consistir en la verdadera fe. El apóstata está perfectamente descrito en <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3 2ti 4:4"> 2 Timoteo 4:3,4 </reference>. Los apóstatas se apartan de la fe, pero no de la profesión exterior del cristianismo <reference osisRef="2ti 3:5"> 2 Timoteo 3:5 </reference> . Los maestros apóstatas se describen en; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3"> 2 Timoteo 4:3 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:1-19"> 2 Pedro 2:1-19 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="jude 1:4 jude 1:8 jude 1:11-13 jude 1:16"> Judas 1:4,8,11-13,16 </reference> . </item> </list> <div sID="gen5003" type="x-p"/> Apostasía en la iglesia, como en Israel <reference osisRef="isa 1:5 isa 1:6"> Isaías 1:5,6 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="isa 5:5-7"> 5:5-7 </reference> es irremediable, y espera juicio; <reference osisRef="2th 2:10-12"> 2 Tesalonicenses 2:10-12 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="2pe 2:17 2pe 2:21"> 2 Pedro 2:17,21 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="jude 1:11-15"> Judas 1:11-15 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="re 3:14-16"> Apocalipsis 3:14-16 </reference> .

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv149"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Titus</title> <div sID="gen5013" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="tit 1">Read first chapter of Titus</reference><div eID="gen5013" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5014" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="tit 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5014" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5015" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Practically the same with First Timothy<div eID="gen5015" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5016" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Titus has much in common with First Timothy. Both Epistles are concerned with the due order of the churches. The distinction is that in First Timothy sound doctrine is more prominent <reference osisRef="1ti 1:3-10">1 Timothy 1:3-10</reference> in Titus the divine order for the local churches <reference osisRef="tit 1:5">Titus 1:5</reference>. The permanent use of these Epistles lies in this twofold application, on the one hand to churches grown careless as to the truth of God, on the other, to churches careless as to the order of God's house. The importance of this order is made solemnly emphatic in that the tests by which true elders and deacons may be known are repeated ; <reference osisRef="1ti 3:1-7">1 Timothy 3:1-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 1:6-9">Titus 1:6-9</reference>.<div eID="gen5016" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5017" type="x-p"/> There are two divisions:<div eID="gen5017" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The qualifications and functions of elders, 1:1-16.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The pastoral work of the true elder, 2:1-3,15.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5018" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv149"/> <hi type="bold">Saviour</hi> <div eID="gen5018" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5019" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold"> queriendo </hi> <div eID="gen5019" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5020" type="x-p"/> No se trata en absoluto de la presencia en la asamblea de personas que tengan cualidades de ancianos, hechos supervisores por el Espíritu Santo <reference osisRef="ac 20:28"> Hechos 20:28 </reference> que tales personas estuvieran en las iglesias de Creta se supone; la cuestión es enteramente una cuestión del nombramiento de tales personas. Estas asambleas no carecían de ancianos; pero estaban "faltos", en el sentido de que no fueron debidamente designados. Hay un progreso de doctrina con respecto al nombramiento de ancianos. Cf. v.5, nota. <div eID="gen5020" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5021" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold"> ancianos </hi> <div eID="gen5021" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5022" type="x-p"/> Anciano (presbuteros) y obispo (episcopos = "superintendente") designan el mismo oficio (cf <reference osisRef="tit 1:7"> Tito 1:7 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ac 20:17"> Hechos 20:17 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ac 20:28"> 20:28 </reference> el primero se refiere al hombre, el segundo a una función del cargo. El liderazgo en las iglesias locales apostólicas siempre fue plural. No hay caso de un anciano en una iglesia local. Las funciones de los ancianos son: gobernar el cuerpo de la verdad revelada de la perversión y el error. <reference osisRef="tit 1:9"> Tito 1:9 </reference> para "supervisar" la iglesia como pastor de su rebaño ; Hebreos 13:17 </reference> ; Los ancianos son hechos o "establecidos" en las iglesias por el Espíritu Santo <reference osisRef="ac 20:28"> Hechos 20:28 </reference> pero se pone gran énfasis en su debido nombramiento <reference osisRef="ac 14:23"> Hechos 14:23 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="tit 1:5"> Tito 1:5 </reference> ; προχειροτονέω </w> ," "elegir", "designar con la mano") por un apóstol; ej. <reference osisRef="ac 14:23"> Hechos 14:23 </reference> pero en Tito y Primera Timoteo las calificaciones de un anciano se vuelven parte de las Escrituras para guiar a las iglesias en tal nombramiento. <reference osisRef="1ti 3:1-7"> 1 Timoteo 3:1-7</reference><chapter eID="Titus.1"/><div eID="gen5022" type="x-p"/>.

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv150"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Philemon</title> <div sID="gen5033" type="x-p"/> SCOFIELD REFERENCE NOTES (Old Scofield 1917 Edition)<div eID="gen5033" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5034" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="phm 1">Read first chapter of Philemon</reference><div eID="gen5034" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5035" type="x-p"/> The Epistle of Paul the Apostle to Philemon<div eID="gen5035" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5036" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Paul (<reference osisRef="phm 1:1"> 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5036" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5037" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 64. It is one of the Prison Epistles. See Introductions to Ephesians and Colossians.<div eID="gen5037" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5038" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Onesimus ("profitable"), a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colosse, had robbed his master and fled to Rome. There he became a convert through Paul, who sent him back to Philemon with this letter. It is of priceless value as a teaching<div eID="gen5038" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) in practical righteousness;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) in Christian brotherhood;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) in Christian courtesy;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) in the law of love.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5039" type="x-p"/> The divisions are four<div eID="gen5039" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5040" type="x-p"/> I. Greeting 1-3.<div eID="gen5040" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5041" type="x-p"/> II. The character of Philemon, 4-7.<div eID="gen5041" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5042" type="x-p"/> III. Intercession for Onesimus, 8-21.<div eID="gen5042" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5043" type="x-p"/> IV. Salutations and conclusion, 22-25. <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv150"/><hi type="bold">account</hi><div eID="gen5043" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5044" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="phm 1:17 phm 1:18">Philemon 1:17,18</reference> perfectly illustrate imputation: "Receive him as myself"--reckon to him my merit; "If he hath wronged thee or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account"-- reckon to me his demerit.<div eID="gen5044" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5045" type="x-p"/> See "Imputation," <reference osisRef="le 25:50">Leviticus 25:50</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Jas 2:23">James 2:23</reference>")</hi>. <chapter eID="Phlm.1"/><div eID="gen5045" type="x-p"/> <div canonical="true" eID="gen5032" osisID="Phlm" type="book"/>
<div canonical="true" osisID="Heb" sID="gen5046" type="book"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc1"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc2"/> <milestone n="" type="x-usfm-toc3"/>
<chapter n="1" osisID="Heb.1" sID="Heb.1"/>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv151"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - Hebrews</title> <div sID="gen5047" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="heb 1">Read first chapter of Hebrews</reference><div eID="gen5047" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5048" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The authorship of Hebrews has been in controversy from the earliest times. The book is anonymous, but the reference in <reference osisRef="2pe 3:15">2 Peter 3:15</reference> seems conclusive that Paul was the writer. See also <reference osisRef="heb 13:23">Hebrews 13:23</reference>. All agree that, whether by Paul or another, the point of view is Pauline. We undoubtedly have here the method of Paul's synagogue addresses. No book of Scripture more fully authenticates itself as inspired.<div eID="gen5048" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5049" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: From internal evidence it is clear that Hebrews was written before the destruction of the Temple, A.D. 70 (cf <reference osisRef="heb 10:11">Hebrews 10:11</reference>).<div eID="gen5049" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5050" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: The doctrinal passages reveal the purpose of the book. It was written with a twofold intent:<div eID="gen5050" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">To confirm Jewish Christians by showing that Judaism had come to an end through the fulfilment by Christ of the whole purpose of the law; and</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The hortatory passages show that the writer had in view the danger ever present to Jewish professed believers of either lapsing back into Judaism, or of pausing short of true faith in Jesus Christ. It is clear from the Acts that even the strongest of the believers in Palestine were held to a strange mingling of Judaism and Christianity (e.g. Acts21:18-24 and that snare would be especially apt to entangle professed Christians amongst the Jews of the dispersion.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5051" type="x-p"/> The key-word is "better." Hebrews is a series of contrasts between the good things of Judaism and the better things of Christ. Christ is "better" than angels, than Moses, than Joshua, than Aaron; and the New Covenant than the Mosaic Covenant. Church truth does not appear, the ground of gathering only being stated (<reference osisRef="heb 13:13">Hebrews 13:13</reference>). The whole sphere of Christian profession is before the writer; hence exhortations necessary to warn and alarm a mere professor.<div eID="gen5051" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5052" type="x-p"/> Hebrews is in six divisions, but these include five parenthetic passages of exhortation.<div eID="gen5052" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The great salvation1:1-2:18 (2:1-4, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rest of God, 3:1-4:16 (all parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Our great High Priest, 5:1-8,6 (5:11-6:12, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The new covenant and the heavenly sanctuary, 8:7-10:39 (10:26-39, parenthetic).</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The superiority of the faith way, 11:1-40.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The worship and walk of the believer-priest, 12:1-13:25 (12:3-17, parenthetic).</item> </list> <div sID="gen5053" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv151"/> <hi type="bold">angels</hi> <div eID="gen5053" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5054" type="x-p"/> Angel, Summary: Angel, "messenger," is used of God, of men, and of an order of created spiritual beings whose chief attributes are strength and wisdom. <reference osisRef="2sa 14:20">2 Samuel 14:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 103:20">Psalms 103:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 104:4"> 104:4</reference>. In the O.T. the expression "the angel of the Lord" (sometimes "of God") usually implies the presence of Deity in angelic form. ; <reference osisRef="ge 16:1-13">Genesis 16:1-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 21:17-19"> 21:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 22:11-16">Genesis 22:11-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 31:11-13"> 31:11-13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2-4">Exodus 3:2-4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 2:1">Judges 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 6:12-16"> 6:12-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 13:3-22"> 13:3-22</reference> <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mal 3:1">Malachi 3:1</reference>")</hi>. The word "angel" is used of men in ; <reference osisRef="lu 7:24">Luke 7:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:25">James 2:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:20">Revelation 1:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 2:1 re 2:8 re 2:12 re 2:18"> 2:1,8,12,18</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 3:1 re 3:7 re 3:14"> 3:1,7,14</reference> In <reference osisRef="re 8:3-5">Revelation 8:3-5</reference>. Christ is evidently meant. Sometimes angel is used of the spirit of man. ; <reference osisRef="mt 18:10">Matthew 18:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:15">Acts 12:15</reference>. Though angels are spirits ; <reference osisRef="ps 104:4">Psalms 104:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 1:14">Hebrews 1:14</reference> power is given them to become visible in the semblance of human form. <reference osisRef="ge 19:1">Genesis 19:1</reference> cf ; <reference osisRef="ge 19:5">Genesis 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 3:2">Exodus 3:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="nu 22:22-31">Numbers 22:22-31</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 2:1">Judges 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 6:11 jud 6:22"> 6:11,22</reference>; <reference osisRef="jud 13:3 jud 13:6"> 13:3,6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1ch 21:16 1ch 21:20">1 Chronicles 21:16,20</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 1:20">Matthew 1:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:26">Luke 1:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 20:12">John 20:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 7:30">Acts 7:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:7 ac 12:8"> 12:7,8,</reference> etc.). The word is always used in the masculine gender, though sex, in the human sense, is never ascribed to angels. ; <reference osisRef="mt 22:30">Matthew 22:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="mr 12:25">Mark 12:25</reference>. They are exceedingly numerous. ; <reference osisRef="mt 26:53">Matthew 26:53</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:22">Hebrews 12:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 5:11">Revelation 5:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 68:17">Psalms 68:17</reference>. The power is inconceivable. <reference osisRef="2ki 19:35">2 Kings 19:35</reference>. Their place is about the throne of God. ; <reference osisRef="re 5:11">Revelation 5:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 7:11"> 7:11</reference>. Their relation to the believer is that of "ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation," and this ministry has reference largely to the physical safety and well-being of believers. ; <reference osisRef="1ki 19:5">1 Kings 19:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 34:7">Psalms 34:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 91:11"> 91:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 6:22">Daniel 6:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 2:13 mt 2:19">Matthew 2:13,19</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 4:11"> 4:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:43">Luke 22:43</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 5:19">Acts 5:19</reference>; <reference osisRef="ac 12:7-10">Acts 12:7-10</reference>. From ; <reference osisRef="heb 1:14">Hebrews 1:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="mt 18:10">Matthew 18:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ps 91:11">Psalms 91:11</reference> it would seem that this care for the heirs of salvation begins in infancy and continues through life. The angels observe us ; <reference osisRef="1co 4:9">1 Corinthians 4:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:10">Ephesians 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ec 5:6">Ecclesiastes 5:6</reference> a fact which should influence conduct. They receive departing saints. <reference osisRef="lu 16:22">Luke 16:22</reference>. Man is made "a little lower than the angels," and in incarnation Christ took "for a little "time" this lower place. ; <reference osisRef="ps 8:4 ps 8:5">Psalms 8:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 2:6 heb 2:9">Hebrews 2:6,9</reference> that He might lift the believer into His own sphere above angels. <reference osisRef="heb 2:9 heb 2:10">Hebrews 2:9,10</reference>. The angels are to accompany Christ in His second advent. <reference osisRef="mt 25:31">Matthew 25:31</reference>. To them will be committed the preparation of the judgment of the nations. <reference osisRef="mt 13:30 mt 13:39 mt 13:41 mt 13:42">Matthew 13:30,39,41,42</reference>. See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:mt 25:32">Matthew 25:32</reference>". The kingdom-age is not to be subject to angels, but to Christ and those for whom He was made a little lower than the angels. <reference osisRef="heb 2:5">Hebrews 2:5</reference> An archangel, Michael, is mentioned as having a particular relation to Israel and to the resurrections. ; <reference osisRef="da 10:13 da 10:21">Daniel 10:13,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 12:1 da 12:2"> 12:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:9">Jude 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 4:16">1 Thessalonians 4:16</reference>. The only other angel whose name is revealed Gabriel, was employed in the most distinguished services. ; <reference osisRef="da 8:16">Daniel 8:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="da 9:21"> 9:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 1:19 lu 1:26">Luke 1:19,26</reference>.<div eID="gen5054" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5055" type="x-p"/> Fallen angels. Two classes of these are mentioned:<div eID="gen5055" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) "The angels which kept not their first estate place, but left their own habitation," are "chained under darkness," awaiting judgment. <reference osisRef="2pe 2:4">2 Peter 2:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="jude 1:6">Jude 1:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 6:3">1 Corinthians 6:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="joh 5:22">John 5:22</reference>. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 6:4">Genesis 6:4</reference>")</hi></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) The angels who have Satan <reference osisRef="ge 3:1">Genesis 3:1</reference> as leader.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5056" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>")</hi>.<div eID="gen5056" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5057" type="x-p"/> The origin of these is nowhere explicitly revealed. They may be identical with the demons.<div eID="gen5057" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5058" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 7:22">Matthew 7:22</reference>")</hi>. For Satan and his angels everlasting fire is prepared. <reference osisRef="mt 25:41">Matthew 25:41</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 20:10">Revelation 20:10</reference>.

<hi type="bold"> Melquisedec </hi> <div eID="gen5085" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5086" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 14:18"> Génesis 14:18 </reference> ") </hi>. <div eID="gen5086" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5087" type="x-p"/> Melquisedec era un tipo adecuado de Cristo como Sumo Sacerdote, porque: <div eID="gen5087" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) era rey-sacerdote <reference osisRef="ge 14:18"> Génesis 14:18 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="zec 6:12 zec 6:13"> Zacarías 6:12,13 </reference> </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) su nombre significa "mi rey es justo" (cf) <reference osisRef="isa 11:5"> Isaías 11:5 </reference> y él era rey de Salem (es decir, "paz", cf <reference osisRef="isa 11:6-9"> Isaías 11:6-9 </reference> .) </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) no tuvo (registrado) "principio de días" (cf) <reference osisRef="joh 1:1"> Juan 1:1 </reference> ni "fin de vida" (cf); <reference osisRef="ro 6:9"> Romanos 6:9 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 7:23-25"> Hebreos 7:23-25, </reference> ni </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) fue hecho sumo sacerdote por nombramiento humano <reference osisRef="ps 110:4"> Salmos 110:4 </reference> . Pero el contraste entre el sumo sacerdocio de Melquisedec y Aarón es sólo en cuanto a persona, "orden" (o nombramiento) y duración. En Su obra, Cristo sigue el modelo Aarónico, cuya "sombra" Cristo era la sustancia. ; <reference osisRef="heb 8:1-6"> Hebreos 8:1-6 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 9:1-28"> 9:1-28 </reference>. </item> </list>

<div sID="gen5104" type="x-p"/><chapter n="8" osisID="Heb.8" sID="Heb.8"/>

El Nuevo Pacto, Resumen: <div eID="gen5104" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) "Mejor" que el pacto mosaico no moralmente, sino eficazmente <reference osisRef="heb 7:19"> Hebreos 7:19 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ro 8:3 ro 8:4"> Romanos 8:3,4 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) Establecido sobre promesas "mejores" (es decir, incondicionales). En el Pacto Mosaico Dios dijo: "Si queréis" <reference osisRef="ex 19:5"> Éxodo 19:5, </reference> en el Nuevo Pacto Él dice: "Yo haré" <reference osisRef="heb 8:10 heb 8:12"> Hebreos 8:10,12 </reference>. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) Bajo el Pacto Mosaico la obediencia surgía del miedo <reference osisRef="heb 2:2"> Hebreos 2:2 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 12:25-27"> 12:25-27 </reference> bajo lo Nuevo de corazón y mente dispuestos <reference osisRef="heb 8:10"> Hebreos 8:10 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) El Nuevo Pacto asegura la revelación personal del Señor a cada creyente <reference osisRef="heb 8:11"> Hebreos 8:11 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (5) el completo olvido de los pecados <reference osisRef="heb 8:12"> Hebreos 8:12 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 10:17"> 10:17 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 10:3"> 10:3 </reference>. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (6) descansa sobre una redención cumplida <reference osisRef="mt 26:27 mt 26:28"> Mateo 26:27,28 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 11:25"> 1 Corintios 11:25 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 9:11-12 heb 9:18-23"> Hebreos 9:11-12,18-23 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (7) y asegura la perpetuidad, la futura conversión y la bendición de Israel. <reference osisRef="jer 31:31-40"> Jeremías 31:31-40 </reference> . Véase también "Reino (A.T.)" y <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17"> 2 Samuel 7:8-17 </reference> . </item> </list> <div sID="gen5105" type="x-p"/> El Nuevo Pacto es el octavo, hablando así de resurrección y de plenitud eterna. <div eID="gen5105" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5106" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold"> Pacto </hi> <div eID="gen5106" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5107" type="x-p"/> I. Los Ocho Pactos, Resumen: <div eID="gen5107" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) El Pacto Edénico <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 1:26"> Génesis 1:26 </reference> ") </hi> condicionó la vida del hombre en inocencia. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) El Pacto Adámico <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 3:14"> Génesis 3:14 </reference> ") </hi> condiciona la vida del hombre caído y da promesa de un Redentor. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) El Pacto Noé <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1"> Génesis 9:1 </reference> ") </hi> . establece el principio del gobierno humano. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) El Pacto Abrahámico <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 15:18"> Génesis 15:18 </reference> ") </hi> funda la nación de Israel y confirma, con adiciones específicas, la promesa adámica de redención. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (5) El Pacto Mosaico <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ex 19:25"> Éxodo 19:25 </reference>") </hi>. condena a todos los hombres, "por cuanto todos pecaron". </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (6) El Pacto Palestino <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:De 30:3"> Deuteronomio 30:3 </reference> ") </hi> asegura la restauración y conversión final de Israel. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (7) El Pacto Davídico <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:2Sa 7:16"> 2 Samuel 7:16 </reference> ") </hi> establece la perpetuidad de la familia davídica (cumplida en Cristo), <reference osisRef="mt 1:1"> Mateo 1:1 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33"> Lucas 1:31-33, </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ro 1:3"> Romanos 1:3 </reference> y del reino davídico, sobre Israel y sobre toda la tierra; ser cumplido en y por Cristo; <reference osisRef="2sa 7:8-17"> 2 Samuel 7:8-17 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="zec 12:8"> Zacarías 12:8 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33"> Lucas 1:31-33 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ac 15:14-17"> Hechos 15:14-17 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 15:24"> 1 Corintios 15:24 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (8) El Nuevo pacto descansa sobre el sacrificio de Cristo, y asegura la bienaventuranza eterna, bajo el Pacto Abrahámico <reference osisRef="ga 3:13-29"> Gálatas 3:13-29 </reference> de todos los que creen. Es absolutamente incondicional y, dado que no compromete ninguna responsabilidad hacia el hombre, es final e irreversible. </item> </list> <div sID="gen5108" type="x-p"/> II. La relación de Cristo con los ocho pactos es la siguiente: <div eID="gen5108" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) Con el Pacto Edénico, Cristo, como el "segundo Hombre", el "último Adán" <reference osisRef="1co 15:45-47"> 1 Corintios 15:45-47 </reference> toma el lugar sobre todas las cosas que el primer Adán perdió; <reference osisRef="col 2:10"> Colosenses 2:10 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="heb 2:7-8"> Hebreos 2:7-8 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) Él es la “Simiente de la mujer” del Pacto Adámico <reference osisRef="ge 3:15"> Génesis 3:15 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 12:31"> Juan 12:31 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:8"> 1 Juan 3:8 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ga 4:4"> Gálatas 4:4 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="re 20:10"> Apocalipsis 20:10 </reference> y cumplió sus condiciones de trabajo <reference osisRef="mr 6:3"> Marcos 6:3 </reference> y obediencia. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) Como hijo mayor de Sem, en Él se cumplió supremamente la promesa hecha a Sem en el Pacto Noé. <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Ge 9:1"> Génesis 9:1 </reference> ") </hi> <reference osisRef="col 2:9"> Colosenses 2:9 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) Él es la "Simiente a quien fueron hechas las promesas" en el Pacto Abrahámico; el hijo de Abraham obediente hasta la muerte <reference osisRef="ge 22:18"> Génesis 22:18 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ga 3:16"> Gálatas 3:16 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="php 2:8"> Filipenses 2:8 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (5) Vivió sin pecado bajo la pacto mosaico y llevó por nosotros su maldición. <reference osisRef="ga 3:10-13"> Gálatas 3:10-13 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (6) Vivió obedientemente como judío en la tierra bajo el Pacto Palestino, y aun así cumplirá sus amables promesas <reference osisRef="de 28:1-de 30:9"> Deuteronomio 28:1-30:9 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (7) Él es la "Simiente", "Heredero" y "Rey" bajo el Pacto Davídico <reference osisRef="mt 1:1"> Mateo 1:1 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="lu 1:31-33"> Lucas 1:31-33 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (8) Su sacrificio es el fundamento del Nuevo Pacto <reference osisRef="mt 26:28"> Mateo 26:28 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 11:25"> 1 Corintios 11:25 </reference> . </item> </list>

<hi type="bold"> die </hi> <div eID="gen5119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5120" type="x-p"/> Muerte física, Resumen: <div eID="gen5120" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) La muerte física es consecuencia del pecado <reference osisRef="ge 3:19"> Génesis 3:19 </reference> y la universalidad de la muerte prueba la universalidad del pecado <reference osisRef="ro 5:12-14"> Romanos 5:12-14 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) La muerte física afecta sólo al cuerpo, y no es cesación de la vida ni de la conciencia <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Hab 2:5"> Habacuc 2:5 </reference>") </hi>. Véase Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:lu 16:23"> Lucas 16:23 </reference>". <reference osisRef="re 6:9 re 6:10"> Apocalipsis 6:9,10 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) Toda muerte física termina en la resurrección del cuerpo. Ver "Resurrección" Trabajo <reference osisRef="job 19:25"> 19:25 </reference>. <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:1Co 15:52"> 1 Corintios 15:52 </reference>") </hi>. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) Debido a que la muerte física es consecuencia del pecado, no es inevitable para los redimidos <reference osisRef="ge 5:24"> Génesis 5:24 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 15:51 1co 15:52"> 1 Corintios 15:51,52 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1th 4:15-17"> 1 Tesalonicenses 4:15-17 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (5) La muerte física tiene para el creyente una calificación peculiar. Se le llama "dormir", porque su cuerpo puede ser "despertado" en cualquier momento <reference osisRef="php 3:20 php 3:21"> Filipenses 3:20,21 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1th 4:14-18"> 1 Tesalonicenses 4:14-18 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (6) El alma y el espíritu viven, independientemente de la muerte del cuerpo, que se describe como un "tabernáculo" (tienda), en el que habita el "yo", y que puede ser despojado <reference osisRef="2co 5:1-8"> 2 Corintios 5:1-8 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 15:42-44"> 1 Corintios 15:42-44 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="2pe 1:13-15"> 2 Pedro 1:13-15 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (7) A la muerte del creyente, él es "revestido" con una "casa del cielo" en espera de la resurrección de la "casa terrenal", y de inmediato está "con el Señor". <reference osisRef="2co 5:1-8"> 2 Corintios 5:1-8 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="php 1:23"> Filipenses 1:23 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="lu 23:43"> Lucas 23:43 </reference> . </item> </list> <div sID="gen5121" type="x-p"/> En cuanto a la muerte de Cristo, <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 27:50"> Mateo 27:50 </reference>") </hi>.

<hi type="bold"> fe </hi> <div eID="gen5152" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5153" type="x-p"/> La esencia de la fe consiste en recibir lo que Dios ha revelado, y puede definirse como esa confianza en el Dios de las Escrituras y en Jesucristo a quien él ha enviado, que lo recibe como Salvador y Señor, e impulsa a la obediencia amorosa y a las buenas obras <reference osisRef="joh 1:12"> Juan 1:12 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="jas 2:14-26"> Santiago 2:14-26 </reference> . Los usos particulares de la fe dan lugar a sus definiciones secundarias: <div eID="gen5153" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) Para la salvación, la fe es confianza personal, aparte de obras meritorias, en el Señor Jesucristo, entregado para nuestras transgresiones, y resucitado para nuestra justificación <reference osisRef="ro 4:5 ro 4:23-25"> Romanos 4:5,23-25 ​​</reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) Como se usa en la oración, la fe es la "confianza que tenemos en él, que si pedimos algo conforme a su voluntad, él nos oye" <reference osisRef="1jo 5:14 1jo 5:15"> 1 Juan 5:14,15 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) Como se usa en referencia a las cosas invisibles de las que habla la Escritura, la fe "les da sustancia", de modo que actuemos según la convicción de su realidad. <reference osisRef="heb 11:1-3"> Hebreos 11:1-3 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) Como principio activo en la vida, los usos de la fe se ilustran en <reference osisRef="heb 11:1-39"> Hebreos 11:1-39 </reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv155"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - James</title> <div sID="gen5178" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="jas 1">Read first chapter of James</reference><div eID="gen5178" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5179" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: James <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 4:21">Matthew 4:21</reference>")</hi> , called "the Just" mentioned by Paul with Cephas and John as "pillars" in the church at Jerusalem <reference osisRef="ga 2:9">Galatians 2:9</reference>. He seems to have been, as a religious man, austere, legal, ceremonial <reference osisRef="ac 21:18-24">Acts 21:18-24</reference>.<div eID="gen5179" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5180" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Tradition fixes the martyrdom of James in the year 62, but his Epistle shows no trace of the larger revelations concerning the church and the distinctive doctrines of grace made through the Apostle Paul, nor even of the discussion concerning the relation of Gentile converts to the law of Moses, which culminated in the first council (Ac 15.), over which James presided. This presumes the very early date of James, which may confidently be set down as "the first Epistle to Christians."--Weston.<div eID="gen5180" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5181" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: By "the twelve tribes scattered abroad" we are to understand, not Jews, but Christian Jews of the Dispersion. The church began with such <reference osisRef="ac 2:5-11">Acts 2:5-11</reference> and James, who seems not to have left Jerusalem, would feel a particular pastoral responsibility for these scattered sheep. They still resorted to the synagogues, or called their own assemblies by that name <reference osisRef="jas 2:2">James 2:2,</reference> where "assembly" is "synagogue" in the Gr.). It appears from <reference osisRef="jas 2:1-8">James 2:1-8</reference> that they still held the synagogue courts for the trial of causes arising amongst themselves. The Epistle, then, is elementary in the extreme. To suppose that <reference osisRef="jas 2:14-26">James 2:14-26</reference> is a polemic against Paul's doctrine of justification is absurd. Neither Galatians nor Romans was yet written.<div eID="gen5181" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5182" type="x-p"/> James' theme, then, is "religion" (Gr., threskeia, "outward religious service") as the expression and proof of faith. He does not exalt works as against faith, but faith as producing works. His style is that of the Wisdom-books of the O.T.<div eID="gen5182" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5183" type="x-p"/> The divisions are five:<div eID="gen5183" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The testing of faith1:1-2:26</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The reality of faith tested by the tongue, 3:1-18</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rebuke of worldliness, 4:1-17</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The rich warned5</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Hortatory</item> </list> <div sID="gen5184" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv155"/> <hi type="bold">perfect</hi> <div eID="gen5184" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5185" type="x-p"/> mature and complete. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Mt 5:48">Matthew 5:48</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold"> tentado </hi> <div eID="gen5185" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5186" type="x-p"/> "Tentación" se usa en dos sentidos: <div eID="gen5186" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) Solicitud al mal (p. ej. <reference osisRef="ge 3:1-6"> Génesis 3:1-6 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="mt 4:1"> Mateo 4:1 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 10:13"> 1 Corintios 10:13 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="2co 11:3 2co 11:4"> 2 Corintios 11:3,4 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="jas 1:14"> Santiago 1:14 </reference> ). </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) Pruebas bajo prueba (p. ej.) <reference osisRef="ge 22:1"> Génesis 22:1 </reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 22:28"> Lucas 22:28 </reference> Cf <reference osisRef="lu 4:2"> Lucas 4:2, </reference> Cf <reference osisRef="mt 6:13"> Mateo 6:13 </reference> (solicitud al mal) y <reference osisRef="1pe 1:6"> 1 Pedro 1:6 </reference> (prueba bajo prueba). </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv158"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 1 Peter</title> <div sID="gen5226" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1pe 1">Read first chapter of 1 Peter</reference><div eID="gen5226" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5227" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Peter (<reference osisRef="1pe 1:1">1 Peter 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5227" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5228" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 60. That "Babylon" refers to the former city on the Euphrates, or to Rome, cannot be inferred from <reference osisRef="1pe 5:13">1 Peter 5:13</reference>. The text is obscure.<div eID="gen5228" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5229" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: While Peter undoubtedly has scattered Jewish believers in mind, his Epistles comprehend Gentile believers also (<reference osisRef="1pe 2:10">1 Peter 2:10</reference>). The present Epistle, written from a church on Gentile ground (<reference osisRef="1pe 5:13">1 Peter 5:13</reference>), presents all the foundational truths of the Christian faith, with special emphasis on the atonement. The distinctive note of First Peter is preparation for victory over suffering. The last-name word occurs about fifteen times, and is the key-word to the Epistle.<div eID="gen5229" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5230" type="x-p"/> The Epistle is in three parts:<div eID="gen5230" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Christian suffering and conduct in the light of full salvation, 1:1-2:8</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The believer's life in view of his sevenfold position, and of the vicarious suffering of Christ, 2:9-4:19</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Christian service in the light of the coming of the Chief Shepherd, 5:1-14</item> </list> <div sID="gen5231" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv158"/> <hi type="bold">sins</hi> <div eID="gen5231" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5232" type="x-p"/> Sin. <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:23">Romans 3:23</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold"> Elegir </hi> <div eID="gen5232" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5233" type="x-p"/> Elección, Resumen: En ambos Testamentos las palabras hebreas y griegas se traducen como "elegir", "elección", "elegir", "escogido". En todos los casos significan, simplemente, "elegido" o "elegir"; y se utilizan para elecciones tanto humanas como divinas. <div eID="gen5233" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) En el último uso, elección es: (a) corporativa, como de la nación de Israel, o la iglesia <reference osisRef="isa 45:4"> Isaías 45:4 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="eph 1:4"> Efesios 1:4 </reference> y (b) individual <reference osisRef="1pe 1:2"> 1 Pedro 1:2 </reference> </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) La elección es según la presciencia de Dios <reference osisRef="1pe 1:2"> 1 Pedro 1:2 </reference> y enteramente por gracia, sin mérito humano; <reference osisRef="ro 9:11"> Romanos 9:11 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ro 11:5 ro 11:6"> 11:5,6 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) La elección procede de la voluntad divina <reference osisRef="joh 15:16"> Juan 15:16 </reference> . </item> </list> <div sID="gen5234" type="x-p"/> Elección es, por lo tanto: <div eID="gen5234" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-2"> (1) El acto soberano de Dios en gracia por el cual ciertos son elegidos de entre la humanidad para Sí mismo. <reference osisRef="joh 15:19"> Juan 15:19 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-2"> (2) El acto soberano de Dios por el cual ciertas personas elegidas son elegidas para un servicio distintivo para Él. <reference osisRef="lu 6:13"> Lucas 6:13 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ac 9:15"> Hechos 9:15 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 1:27 1co 1:28"> 1 Corintios 1:27,28 </reference> </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv159"/><div sID="gen5235" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv159"/> <hi type="bold">might</hi> <div eID="gen5235" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5236" type="x-p"/> Suffering, in First Peter, is set in the light of:<div eID="gen5236" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) assured salvation, <reference osisRef="1pe 1:2-5">1 Peter 1:2-5</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) the greater glory at Christ's appearing, <reference osisRef="1pe 1:7">1 Peter 1:7</reference>;</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) Christ's sufferings and coming glories, <reference osisRef="1pe 1:11">1 Peter 1:11</reference></item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) the believer's association with Him in both, <reference osisRef="1pe 2:20 1pe 2:21">1 Peter 2:20,21</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 3:17 1pe 3:18"> 3:17,18</reference> <reference osisRef="1pe 4:12 1pe 4:13"> 4:12,13</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) the purifying effect of suffering, <reference osisRef="1pe 1:7">1 Peter 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 4:1 1pe 4:2"> 4:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 5:10"> 5:10</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(6) that Christ is now glorified in the believer's patient suffering, <reference osisRef="1pe 4:16">1 Peter 4:16</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(7) that suffering is disciplinary, <reference osisRef="1pe 4:17-19">1 Peter 4:17-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 11:31 1co 11:32">1 Corinthians 11:31,32</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:5-13">Hebrews 12:5-13</reference>. </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv160"/><div sID="gen5237" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv160"/> <hi type="bold">salvation</hi> <div eID="gen5237" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5238" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 1:16">Romans 1:16</reference>")</hi>.

<hi type="bold"> por la gracia </hi> <div eID="gen5238" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5239" type="x-p"/> Gracia (en salvación). <reference osisRef="1pe 5:12"> 1 Pedro 5:12 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ro 3:24"> Romanos 3:24 </reference> <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17"> Juan 1:17 </reference> ") </hi> .

<hi type="bold"> redimido </hi> <div eID="gen5519" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5520" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Ro 3:24"> Romanos 3:24 </reference>") </hi>.

<hi type="bold"> preordenado </hi> <div eID="gen5240" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5241" type="x-p"/> El orden divino es presciencia, elección, predestinación. Que la presciencia determina la elección o elección queda claro en <reference osisRef="1pe 1:2"> 1 Pedro 1:2 </reference> y la predestinación es el cumplimiento de la elección. "La elección mira hacia atrás, a la presciencia; la predestinación, hacia el destino". Pero la Escritura en ninguna parte declara qué es lo que en la presciencia divina determina la elección y predestinación divinas. Los preconocidos son elegidos, y los elegidos son predestinados, y esta elección es segura para todo creyente por el solo hecho de que crea <reference osisRef="1th 1:4 1th 1:5"> 1 Tesalonicenses 1:4,5 </reference> <div eID="gen5241" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5242" type="x-p"/> Ver Predestinación <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Eph 1:5"> Efesios 1:5 </reference> ") </hi> . <chapter eID="1Pet.1"/> <div eID="gen5242" type="x-p"/>
<div sID="gen5243" type="x-p"/> <chapter n="2" osisID="1Pet.2" sID="1Pet.2"/>

<hi type="bold"> piedra de tropiezo </hi> <div eID="gen5243" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5244" type="x-p"/> Cristo crucificado es la Roca: <div eID="gen5244" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1"> (1) Herido para que el Espíritu de vida fluya de Él a todos los que quieran beber <reference osisRef="ex 17:6"> Éxodo 17:6 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 10:4"> 1 Corintios 10:4 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 4:13 joh 4:14"> Juan 4:13,14 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 7:37-39"> 7:37-39 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (2) A la iglesia el fundamento y piedra angular principal <reference osisRef="eph 2:20"> Efesios 2:20 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (3) Para los judíos en Su primera venida una “piedra de tropiezo” <reference osisRef="ro 9:32 ro 9:33"> Romanos 9:32,33 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="1co 1:23"> 1 Corintios 1:23 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (4) a Israel en Su segunda venida la "lápida del ángulo" <reference osisRef="zec 4:7"> Zacarías 4:7 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (5) A la potencia mundial gentil la "piedra cortada sin mano" para herir <reference osisRef="da 2:34"> Daniel 2:34 </reference> . </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (6) En el propósito divino la Piedra que, después de la destrucción del poder mundial gentil, debe crecer y llenar la tierra. </item> <item type="x-indent-1"> (7) A los incrédulos la Piedra aplastante del juicio. <reference osisRef="mt 21:44"> Mateo 21:44 </reference> . </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv161"/><div sID="gen5245" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv161"/> <hi type="bold">priesthood</hi> <div eID="gen5245" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5246" type="x-p"/> The New Testament priesthood, Summary:<div eID="gen5246" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(1) Until the law was given the head of each family was the family priest <reference osisRef="ge 8:20">Genesis 8:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 26:25"> 26:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="ge 31:54"> 31:54</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(2) When the law was proposed, the promise to perfect obedience was that Israel would be unto God "a kingdom of priests" <reference osisRef="ex 19:6">Exodus 19:6</reference>. but Israel violated the law, and God shut up the priestly office to the Aaronic family, appointing the tribe of Levi to minister to them, thus constituting the typical priesthood <reference osisRef="ex 28:1">Exodus 28:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(3) In the dispensation of grace, all believers are unconditionally constituted a "kingdom of priests" <reference osisRef="1pe 2:9">1 Peter 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="re 1:6">Revelation 1:6</reference> the distinction which Israel failed to achieve by works. The priesthood of the believer is, therefore, a birthright; just as every descendant of Aaron was born to the priesthood <reference osisRef="heb 5:1">Hebrews 5:1</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">(4) The chief privilege of a priest is access to God. Under law the high priest only could enter "the holiest of all," and that but once a year <reference osisRef="heb 9:7">Hebrews 9:7,</reference> but when Christ died, the veil, type of Christ's human body <reference osisRef="heb 10:20">Hebrews 10:20</reference> was rent, so that now the believer-priests, equally with Christ the High Priest, have access to God in the holiest <reference osisRef="heb 10:19-22">Hebrews 10:19-22</reference>.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5247" type="x-p"/> The high Priest is corporeally there <reference osisRef="heb 4:14-16">Hebrews 4:14-16</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 9:24"> 9:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:19-22"> 10:19-22</reference>.<div eID="gen5247" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">(5) In the exercise of his office the New Testament believer-priest is</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(1) a sacrificer who offers a threefold sacrifice: (a) his own living body. <reference osisRef="ro 12:1">Romans 12:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 2:17">Philippians 2:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:6">2 Timothy 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 3:16">1 John 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 1:27">James 1:27</reference> (b) praise to God, "the fruit of the lips that make mention of His name" (R.V.), to be offered "continually" ; <reference osisRef="heb 13:15">Hebrews 13:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="ex 25:22">Exodus 25:22</reference> "I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat"); (c) his substance ; <reference osisRef="heb 13:16">Hebrews 13:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 12:13">Romans 12:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:6">Galatians 6:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="3jo 1:5-8">3 John 1:5-8</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 13:2">Hebrews 13:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 6:10">Galatians 6:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="tit 3:14">Titus 3:14</reference>.</item> <item type="x-indent-2">(2) The N.T. priest is also an intercessor <reference osisRef="1ti 2:1">1 Timothy 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 4:12">Colossians 4:12</reference> </item> </list>

<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv163"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 2 Peter</title> <div sID="gen5275" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2pe 1">Read first chapter of 2 Peter</reference><div eID="gen5275" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5276" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle Peter (<reference osisRef="2pe 1:1">2 Peter 1:1</reference>)<div eID="gen5276" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5277" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 66<div eID="gen5277" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5278" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Second Peter and Second Timothy have much in common. In both, the writers are aware that martyrdom is near (<reference osisRef="2ti 4:6">2 Timothy 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 1:14">2 Peter 1:14</reference> with ; <reference osisRef="joh 21:18 joh 21:19">John 21:18,19</reference>); both are singularly sustained and joyful; both foresee the apostasy in which the history of the professing church will end. Paul finds that apostasy in its last stage when the so-called laity <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Re 2:6">Revelation 2:6</reference>")</hi> , have become infected (<reference osisRef="2ti 3:1-5">2 Timothy 3:1-5</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 4:3 2ti 4:4"> 4:3,4</reference>); Peter traces the origin of the apostasy to false teachers (<reference osisRef="2pe 2:1-3 2pe 2:15-19">2 Peter 2:1-3,15-19</reference>). In Peter the false teachers deny redemption truth (<reference osisRef="2pe 2:1">2 Peter 2:1</reference>); we shall find in First John a deeper depth--denial of the truth concerning Christ's person (<reference osisRef="1jo 4:1-5">1 John 4:1-5</reference>). In Jude all phases of the apostasy are seen. But in none of these Epistles is the tone one of dejection or pessimism. God and His promises are still the resource of the believer.<div eID="gen5278" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5279" type="x-p"/> The Epistle is in four divisions:<div eID="gen5279" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The great Christian virtues, 1:1-14</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The Scriptures exalted, 1:15-21</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Warnings concerning apostate teachers, 2:1-22</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The second coming of Christ and the day of Jehovah, 3:1-18</item> </list> <div sID="gen5280" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv163"/> <hi type="bold">grace</hi> <div eID="gen5280" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5281" type="x-p"/> Grace (imparted). <reference osisRef="ro 6:1">Romans 6:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="2pe 3:18">2 Peter 3:18</reference>

<hi type="bold"> monte santo </hi> <div eID="gen5283" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5284" type="x-p"/> Cuando la referencia es a cosas, el significado de "santo" o "santificado" es, simplemente, apartado para el uso de Dios, o vuelto sagrado por la presencia divina.

<hi type="bold"> donde </hi> <div eID="gen5284" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5285" type="x-p"/> Es decir, más seguro por el cumplimiento en parte. La profecía cumplida es una prueba de inspiración porque las predicciones de las Escrituras sobre eventos futuros fueron pronunciadas mucho antes de que ocurrieran, que ninguna sagacidad o previsión meramente humana podría haberlas anticipado, y estas predicciones son tan detalladas, minuciosas y específicas, que excluyen la posibilidad de que fueran meras conjeturas afortunadas. Cientos de predicciones acerca de Israel, la tierra de Canaán, Babilonia, Asiria, Egipto y numerosos personajes (tan antiguas, tan singulares, tan aparentemente improbables, así como tan detalladas y definidas que ningún mortal podría haberlas anticipado) han sido cumplidas por los elementos y por hombres que las ignoraban, o que no creían en ellas, o que luchaban con frenética desesperación para evitar su cumplimiento. Es cierto, por tanto, que las Escrituras que los contienen son inspiradas. "La profecía nunca fue traída por voluntad humana, sino que los santos hombres de Dios hablaron siendo inspirados por el Espíritu Santo" <reference osisRef="2pe 1:21"> 2 Pedro 1:21 </reference> . <div eID="gen5285" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5286" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold"> un más seguro </hi> O, la palabra de profecía se hizo más segura. <div eID="gen5286" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5287" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold"> lugar oscuro </hi> O, lugar sórdido. <reference osisRef="ps 119:105"> Salmos 119:105 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="joh 1:4 joh 1:9"> Juan 1:4,9 </reference> .

Resumen (ver "Gracia") <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17"> Juan 1:17 </reference> ") </hi> la gracia no es sólo dispensacionalmente un método de trato divino en la salvación <div eID="gen5300" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5301" type="x-p"/> <hi type="italic"> (Ver Scofield " <reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17"> Juan 1:17 </reference> ") </hi> sino que también es el método de Dios en la vida y el servicio del creyente. Como salvo, él "no está bajo la ley, sino bajo la gracia" <reference osisRef="ro 6:14"> Romanos 6:14 </reference> . Habiendo llevado por gracia al creyente a la posición más alta imaginable. <reference osisRef="eph 1:6"> Efesios 1:6 </reference> . Dios obra incesantemente por la gracia para impartirle y perfeccionar en él las gracias correspondientes; <reference osisRef="joh 15:4 joh 15:5"> Juan 15:4,5 </reference> ; <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23"> Gálatas 5:22,23 </reference> . <div eID="gen5301" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5302" type="x-p"/> La gracia, por lo tanto, está relacionada con el servicio <reference osisRef="ro 12:6"> Romanos 12:6 </reference> ; <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv164"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 1 John</title> <div sID="gen5305" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="1jo 1">Read first chapter of 1 John</reference><div eID="gen5305" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5306" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle John, as unbroken tradition affirms, and as internal evidence and comparison with the Gospel of John prove.<div eID="gen5306" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5307" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 90<div eID="gen5307" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5308" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: First John is a family letter from the Father to His "little children" who are in the world. With the possible exception of the Song, it is the most intimate of the inspired writings. The world is viewed as without. The sin of a believer is treated as a child's offence against his Father, and is dealt with as a family matter (<reference osisRef="1jo 1:9">1 John 1:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 2:1"> 2:1</reference>). The moral government of the universe is not in question. The child's sin as an offence against the law had been met in the Cross, and "Jesus Christ the righteous" is now his "Advocate with the Father." John's Gospel leads across the threshold of the Father's house; his first Epistle makes us at home there. A tender word is used for "children," teknia, "born ones," or "bairns." Paul is occupied with our public position as sons; John with our nearness as born-ones of the Father.<div eID="gen5308" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5309" type="x-p"/> First John is in two principal divisions.<div eID="gen5309" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The family with the Father, 1:1-3:24.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The family and the world, 4:1-5:21.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5310" type="x-p"/> There is a secondary analysis in each division of which occurs the phrase, "My little children," as follows:<div eID="gen5310" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">Introductory, the incarnation, 1:1,2.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The little children and fellowship1:3-2:14</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The little children and secular and "religious" world2:15-28.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">How the little children may know each other, 2:29-3:10</item> <item type="x-indent-1">How the little children must live together, 3:11-24.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Parenthetic: How the little children may know false teachers, 4:1-6.</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The little children assured and warned, 4:7-5:21.</item> </list> <div sID="gen5311" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv164"/><hi type="bold">grace</hi> Grace (imparted). Summary (see "Grace,") <hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi> grace is not only dispensationally a method of divine dealing in salvation<div eID="gen5311" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5312" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Joh 1:17">John 1:17</reference>")</hi> but is also the method of God in the believer's life and service. As saved, he is "not under the law, but under grace" <reference osisRef="ro 6:14">Romans 6:14</reference>. Having by grace brought the believer into the highest conceivable position. <reference osisRef="eph 1:6">Ephesians 1:6</reference>. God ceaselessly works through grace, to impart to, and perfect in him, corresponding graces ; <reference osisRef="joh 15:4 joh 15:5">John 15:4,5</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 5:22 ga 5:23">Galatians 5:22,23</reference>.<div eID="gen5312" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5313" type="x-p"/> Grace, therefore, stands connected with service <reference osisRef="ro 12:6">Romans 12:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="ro 15:15 ro 15:16"> 15:15,16</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 1:3-7">1 Corinthians 1:3-7</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 3:10"> 3:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="1co 15:10"> 15:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="2co 12:9 2co 12:10">2 Corinthians 12:9,10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 2:9">Galatians 2:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 3:7 eph 3:8">Ephesians 3:7,8</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:7">Ephesians 4:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="php 1:7">Philippians 1:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="2ti 2:1 2ti 2:2">2 Timothy 2:1,2</reference>; <reference osisRef="1pe 4:10">1 Peter 4:10</reference> with Christian growth ; <reference osisRef="2co 1:12">2 Corinthians 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="eph 4:29">Ephesians 4:29</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 3:16">Colossians 3:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="col 4:6"> 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="2th 1:12">2 Thessalonians 1:12</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 4:16">Hebrews 4:16</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 12:28 heb 12:29"> 12:28,29</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 13:9"> 13:9</reference>; <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv166"/><title type="x-s">Book Introduction - 2 John</title> <div sID="gen5349" type="x-p"/> <reference osisRef="2jo 1">Read first chapter of 2 John</reference><div eID="gen5349" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5350" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">WRITER</hi>: The Apostle John.<div eID="gen5350" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5351" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">DATE</hi>: Probably A.D. 90.<div eID="gen5351" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5352" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">THEME</hi>: Second John gives the essentials of the personal walk of the believer in a day when "many deceivers are entered into the world" (<reference osisRef="2jo 1:7">2 John 1:7</reference>). The key phrase is "the truth," by which John means the body of revealed truth, the Scriptures. The Bible as the only authority for doctrine and life, is the believer's resource in a time of declension and apostasy.<div eID="gen5352" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5353" type="x-p"/> The Epistle in three divisions:<div eID="gen5353" type="x-p"/> <list> <item type="x-indent-1">The pathway of truth and love, vs. 1-6</item> <item type="x-indent-1">The peril of unscriptural ways, vs. 7-11</item> <item type="x-indent-1">Superscription, vs. 12,13</item> </list> <div sID="gen5354" type="x-p"/> <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv166"/> <hi type="bold">that we love one another</hi> <div eID="gen5354" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5355" type="x-p"/> Law (of Christ), Summary: The new "law of Christ" is the divine love, as wrought into the renewed heart by the Holy Spirit <reference osisRef="ro 5:5">Romans 5:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="heb 10:16">Hebrews 10:16</reference> and outflowing in the energy of the Spirit, unforced and spontaneous, toward the objects of the divine love ; <reference osisRef="2co 5:14-20">2 Corinthians 5:14-20</reference>; <reference osisRef="1th 2:7 1th 2:8">1 Thessalonians 2:7,8</reference>. It is, therefore, " the law of liberty" ; <reference osisRef="jas 1:25">James 1:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="jas 2:12"> 2:12</reference> in contrast with the external law of Moses. Moses' law demands love, ; <reference osisRef="le 19:18">Leviticus 19:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="de 6:5">Deuteronomy 6:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="lu 10:27">Luke 10:27</reference> Christ's law is love ; <reference osisRef="ro 5:5">Romans 5:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="1jo 4:7 1jo 4:19 1jo 4:20">1 John 4:7,19,20</reference> and so takes the place of the external law by fulfilling it ; <reference osisRef="ro 13:10">Romans 13:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="ga 5:14">Galatians 5:14</reference>. It is the "law written in the heart" under the New Covenant.<div eID="gen5355" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen5356" type="x-p"/><hi type="italic">(See Scofield "<reference osisRef="Scofield:Heb 8:8">Hebrews 8:8</reference>")</hi>.
